name: Opinions and formal advice
one_line: A J-DEPTH placeholder template for the ADDRESSED, RELIANCE-BEARING statement of legal position - the closing or enforceability opinion letter, the tax opinion with its reliance level, counsel's advice on merits, the response to an auditor's request for information, the board advice memorandum, and the bring-down, reliance-extension and withdrawal letters that maintain them. It is NOT the word `opinion` and NOT a document-type value: it is the only situation in this family whose evidence is a THREE-ROLE, SELF-SUFFICIENT SINGLE ARTEFACT - an addressee block naming a body that the document itself distinguishes from the client, a clause in the document's own words restricting who may rely on it, and the assumptions / qualifications / scope-of-law grammar that makes a conclusion an opinion rather than a report. That structure lets it fire on ONE file where the `law_practice` default requires an exact matter reference repeated across two or more artefacts, and it carries a handling rule no sibling has: the conclusion may never be stored, surfaced or summarised detached from the assumptions and qualifications that bound it. It deliberately does NOT hold the internal research note or authorities list behind the advice (`law_practice.legal-research`), the unaddressed blank-slot model opinion (`law_practice.precedent-bank`), a court's own opinion or judgment (`law_practice.orders-and-judgments`), advice given in the running text of an email (`law_practice.matter-correspondence`), or an opinion the HOLDER received about the holder's own position (`legal.personal-legal-matters`). Declares no field rows and no folder dimensions under PR-6.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key_works: A GENUINE HOLE, RAISED ONCE AND ONLY BECAUSE THIS ROW'S WHOLE CLAIM RESTS ON IT - and raised with its own defeat argument attached, so R1c can close it either way. The addressee of a formal opinion is the party ENTITLED TO RELY, and in this family that party is routinely NOT the client: an agent bank and a syndicate of lenders on a financing opinion, a named audit firm on a response to an auditor's request, a purchaser's counsel on a transaction opinion, a regulator on a compliance opinion. None of the schema anchor's six proposals can hold that person. `client` cannot - the document itself distinguishes the two, and an opinion frequently says so in terms (`our client`, `you`). `our_firm` is the author half. `subject_of_record`, which `clinical_practice` proposed and `nonprofit` adopted, is the person a record is ABOUT; the addressee is the person a record is TO, and on an enforceability opinion the subject is an instrument and the addressee is a bank - two different slots on the same page. `party` and `counterparty` are not canonical and would be mints. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which this row does not hide: an addressee is a slot on ordinary correspondence too, so a key named for it risks becoming a synonym for `recipient` across the whole roster, and the concept may be better served by keeping the addressee a LITERAL OBSERVATION that never becomes a fact at all - which is what this row does today and what it can keep doing forever if R1c declines.
proposed_fields.preferred_resolution: Preference order: (a) DECLINE and record that the addressee stays a literal observation on the evidence and never becomes a fact - this row is fully functional under that outcome and recommends it if there is any doubt; (b) if adopted, adjudicate ONCE for the whole roster rather than for this family, since email, matter-correspondence and regulatory-submission rows would all reach for it, and seed `destination_eligible` FALSE with the reason on the key: an addressee-named branch publishes that a named bank, auditor or regulator is party to a transaction that has not been announced, which is the same disclosure `law_practice` already refused for `client`. Do NOT permit `relying_party`, `recipient_role`, `opinion_addressee` or `reliance_party` as variants.
proposed_fields.why: The third role that makes this row structurally distinct from its schema's two-role default. It is proposed so the distinction can be argued, not so it can be filed on - and this row prefers the decline.

deterministic: PRECONDITION AND THE ROW'S WHOLE DIFFERENCE FROM ITS SCHEMA'S DEFAULT. `law_practice`'s default requires BOTH (i) an exact matter reference repeated across two or more artefacts and (ii) a separate artefact whose slots split a practitioner role from a client role. This row RELAXES (i) and REPLACES it with an intra-document structure, because a formal opinion routinely arrives alone - one PDF in a closing binder, one advice in a folder with no surrounding apparatus. The substitute is THE ADDRESSEE-AND-RELIANCE PAIR: a labelled addressee block naming a person or body that is not the author, PLUS a clause in the document's own words restricting who may rely on it or take the benefit of it. Both slots, one artefact, and the professional-role separation is satisfied inside the page rather than across the corpus. Everything else here is a refinement of that pair; nothing here fires without it.

THE OPINION GRAMMAR, which is what survives the deletion test - delete every entity name, the word `opinion` and the word `advice`, and this remains: a DOCUMENTS-EXAMINED or MATERIALS-CONSIDERED section, an ASSUMPTIONS section stating facts taken as true and expressly not verified, a QUALIFICATIONS or EXCEPTIONS section, a SCOPE-OF-LAW slot disclaiming every jurisdiction but one, an operative conclusion paragraph, and a date the document speaks as of. The co-occurrence of assumptions-plus-qualifications-plus-scope-of-law is the discriminator: a report has findings and a methodology, an opinion has assumptions it declines to check and exceptions it declines to cover.

A RELIANCE-LEVEL slot - a graded confidence the document states about ITSELF in a labelled position (`will`, `should`, `more likely than not`, `reasonable basis`, `substantial authority`, `good arguable case`, `prospects`). No neighbour in this family produces a document that grades its own conclusion, and it is the tax and merits opinions' cleanest fingerprint. Provenance: inference.

A THIRD-ROLE ADDRESSEE: the addressee block names an entity the SAME document elsewhere distinguishes from the client - `our client`, `the Company`, `the Borrower` in the body against `to the Agent and the Lenders` or `to the Auditors` in the address. Three separately labelled roles on one page is a structure neither `law_practice`'s two-role default nor any sibling produces.

AN AUDITOR-REQUEST RESPONSE structure: addressed to a named audit firm, referencing a request made by the client, enumerating matters to which the practice has devoted substantive attention with a short description of each, and closing with an express limitation on the scope of the response. It is simultaneously an opinion artefact and audit evidence, which is why `finance` is this row's coactivation edge.

AN INSTRUCTED-PROFESSIONAL ADVICE structure: a front sheet naming an advising professional and chambers or firm and a separate INSTRUCTING professional, an `I am asked to advise` or `we have been asked to opine` opening, numbered paragraphs separating the questions asked from the conclusions reached, and a prospects or recommendation paragraph. Note the deliberate seam with the schema anchor's own COUNSEL-INSTRUCTION signal: the anchor's signal is the INSTRUCTIONS front sheet and its bundle index; this row claims the ADVICE that comes back, and where the two are bound into one PDF the file is a candidate for both templates on the same bytes.

A BRING-DOWN, RELIANCE-EXTENSION or WITHDRAWAL structure, and it is the signal no neighbour anywhere on the roster produces: a short letter whose own slots reference an EARLIER OPINION by its date and its addressee, and confirm, extend to a newly named addressee, qualify or withdraw it. A document whose subject is another document's continuing validity is a distinct artefact shape, and it is the reason this row's grouping is a lineage rather than a single file.

AN ARCHIVE MANIFEST, read without unpacking, whose member names show several opinion-shaped documents from SEVERAL DIFFERENT AUTHOR FIRMS under one transaction reference - the closing-opinions bundle. Multiple authors under one anchor is the shape; the directory names are observations and become facts on no member.
needs_llm: Deciding whether the holder GAVE or RECEIVED the advice. The same opinion letter exists in the author's file and in the addressee's file and differs only in which signature block is the holder's. This row is the giver's side; `legal.personal-legal-matters` is the holder-as-advisee side; abstain when the side cannot be cited.

Separating an addressed opinion from the internal research note that produced it, when a note carries a covering line naming a reader. `law_practice.legal-research` owns the authorities survey and the internal analysis; this row owns the document a named outsider may rely on. The presence of a reliance restriction is the intended discriminator, but a terse internal advice may carry one and a sloppy opinion may omit it.

Separating a legal opinion from a consulting or advisory deliverable when BOTH carry an addressee block and a no-third-party-responsibility clause - the collision this row treats as its headline, because the use-limitation clause is universal across professional deliverables and is therefore worthless as evidence on its own.

Deciding whether a copy of a court's own opinion is reference reading, an authority relied on by an accepted matter, or an exhibit. Topic will not separate them; the design's own test is the only one that works - `Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.`

Recognising advice given in unlabelled prose - an attendance note recording oral advice, a strategy email in running text, a scanned handwritten note. The design names this class among the reasons rules are insufficient. Such a file is a `law_practice.matter-correspondence` member unless the addressed-and-reliance structure is present.
Deciding whether a later short letter is a bring-down of a named opinion, a withdrawal of it, or an unrelated covering letter that happens to cite a date.

Judging whether a second opinion reviewing another adviser's advice is this row's artefact or a critique filed as work product, when the reviewing document has an addressee but no assumptions section.
Abstaining whenever the addressee's role cannot be resolved from the artefact itself. `Correct abstention is a successful outcome`.
never_alone: THE WORD `OPINION`, AND ESPECIALLY A JUDICIAL ONE. This is the row's existential strike and the reason the collision fixture exists: a court's decision and a lawyer's advice letter share the word completely, and the judicial one is published, freely downloaded, and present in enormous numbers in exactly the corpora where this row would fire. A caption plus a bench plus an operative disposition and NO addressee block is `law_practice.orders-and-judgments` or reading material; it is never this row.

A LIMITATION-OF-LIABILITY OR NO-THIRD-PARTY-RESPONSIBILITY CLAUSE ALONE. The single most dangerous token here, because it is the row's own headline signal in isolated form and it appears on every consulting report, valuation, building survey, actuarial certificate, audit deliverable and market study ever written. It is evidence only in the PAIR with an addressee block AND the assumptions-and-qualifications grammar.
AN ADDRESSEE BLOCK ALONE. Every letter has one. It resolves nothing about the document's function and names an entity, which is itself a struck token.

A LAW-FIRM LETTERHEAD BESIDE THE WORD `ADVICE`, and more generally a document-type word beside an entity name. This is the two-role escape route `business_operations.organisational-records` closed and `law_practice` restated: a document-type word is not a labelled party, so a firm name and a type word are two struck tokens, not a structure.

A MODAL OR GRADED WORD in free text - `should`, `will`, `more likely than not`, `we consider`, `prospects are good`. The reliance-level signal requires the grade to sit in a labelled position that the document supplies about its own conclusion, not to appear in a sentence.
A NUMBERED-PARAGRAPH LETTER ON PROFESSIONAL LETTERHEAD. Engagement terms, demand letters, complaint responses, planning submissions and insurance declinature letters all have that shape.

A PRIVILEGED, CONFIDENTIAL, ATTORNEY-CLIENT, LEGALLY-PRIVILEGED or WITHOUT-PREJUDICE LEGEND. Inherited from the schema and restated because it is applied to advice more often than to anything else: the product preserves the literal observation and decides no legal status, and the legend is not evidence that the schema, let alone this template, applies.

A DETACHED CONCLUSION SENTENCE - an opinion's operative line quoted in an email, pasted into a chat, or captured in a screenshot. It is a REPORT of advice, not the advice, and treating it as this row's evidence is the specific error that this row's privacy rule exists to prevent: severed from its assumptions and qualifications it is a misstatement of the position it appears to state.

A NAMED BANK, AUDIT FIRM, REGULATOR, CHAMBERS, COUNSEL OR CLIENT. Inherited from the schema in full - a firm name appears as author, as addressee, as opposing counsel, as a cited firm and as an employer.
A FILENAME OR FOLDER containing `opinion`, `advice`, `memo`, `letter`, `counsel` or `legal`. A folder is an unlabelled position and paths stay local.
A SOURCE TYPE OR EXTENSION, including every one this row lists. file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone.

DOWNLOAD-SESSION OR BUNDLE MEMBERSHIP. A set of official-looking PDFs that arrived together is a session - `A session should never be treated as proof of topic` - and a closing bundle qualifies only through the manifest structure above, never through co-arrival.

A SHARED ADDRESSEE ACROSS TWO DOCUMENTS. Stated as a strike rather than a grouping reason because it is the mistake this row invites: one agent bank is the addressee of hundreds of unrelated opinions, and grouping by addressee would build a folder that names a financial institution and enumerates every deal it is in.

proposed_context_terms: for the benefit of the addressees
work_types: tax opinion with a stated reliance level
counsel's advice on merits, quantum or prospects
board, trustee or committee advice memorandum addressed to a named body
regulatory or supervisory opinion addressed to an authority
response to an auditor's request for information
second opinion or review of another adviser's advice
reliance letter extending an existing opinion to a newly named addressee
bring-down, update, qualification or withdrawal of an earlier opinion
grouping_reasons: ONE OPINION ACROSS ITS LIFE: draft, negotiated markup, executed and signed, and then its bring-down, reliance extensions, qualifications and withdrawal - joined by the later documents' own explicit reference to the earlier opinion's date and addressee. This is the row's characteristic group and it is a LINEAGE, which is why the anchor is a stated cross-reference and never a `-final` suffix.

ONE CLOSING'S OPINION SET: several opinions from several different author firms, joined by one exact transaction or matter reference in the bundle manifest or in the opinions' own recitals. `The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent` - a capacity opinion, a tax opinion and a foreign-law opinion say entirely different things and exist for one event.

ONE ADVICE EPISODE: the questions or instructions that were sent, the advice that came back, and the covering note that transmitted it - joined by an exact matter reference. Membership never copies a client, addressee, conclusion or reliance-level fact onto any member.
ONE AUDIT CYCLE'S RESPONSES: the auditor's request, the practice's response and any supplemental or update response, joined by an exact audit period reference supplied by the documents.

NO GROUP AT ALL is normal and correct here. A single opinion letter with nothing around it is complete on its own evidence and is still protected material; `It should not form a supported group when there is no valid anchor`.

NOT grouping reasons, and each of these is a mistake this row specifically invites: a shared ADDRESSEE (one bank sees hundreds of opinions); a shared LEGAL ISSUE or cited authority across two matters; a shared reliance level; a shared author firm; a shared closing date; co-arrival in one download or one bundle.

template.why: EMPTY, and for the schema's three reasons plus one that is this row's own. Inherited: (1) BY CONTRACT a dimension may only branch on a field the schema declares and `law_practice` declares none under PR-6; (2) BY THE SAFETY NEIGHBOUR this material co-activates `legal`, and no deep template unlocks from safety activation; (3) BY DISCLOSURE, since the natural dimensions here are a client and a matter and both publish the existence and subject of a representation. THIS ROW'S OWN ADDITION, and it is the paragraph that differs from the schema anchor's held-as-prose recommendation: the axis this situation most obviously offers is the ADDRESSEE, and it must be refused harder than the client axis. A client-named branch discloses that a named person is in a matter; an ADDRESSEE-named branch discloses a named bank, auditor or regulator AND the transaction they are party to, to a reader who is not the client and never consented - `The default posture must therefore be local-first and data-minimizing.` The second addition is the RELIANCE LEVEL, which looks harmlessly non-identifying and is worse than it looks: a folder literally named for a graded legal confidence sorts a corpus by how weak its positions are, and it would be read by every later process. Function-under-matter still governs if PR-6 ever lifts: an opinion's bring-down or its reliance extension is unintelligible without the opinion it maintains, which is the design's own child-needs-parent argument. NOT TIME-FIRST: this world has at least four unrelated dates on one page - the date the opinion speaks as of, the date of the instrument opined on, the delivery date and the filesystem date - and nothing here is capture-based, so a time-first order would scatter one lineage across calendar folders while claiming an exception this evidence does not support.

sensitivity_why: An opinion states a legal position on a named party's affairs and does so in a document engineered to be handed to an outsider, which makes its exposure profile different from the rest of the family rather than merely severe. Three specific reasons. First, the ADDRESSEE LIST is itself the disclosure: naming an agent bank, a syndicate, an audit firm or a purchaser's counsel discloses that a transaction exists, who is in it, and often that it has not been announced - and those parties are third parties to a third party, with no relationship to the holder at all, which is `law_practice`'s stricter-than-`legal` claim in its sharpest form. Second, the CONTENT is a graded weakness: a reliance level, a qualifications section and a prospects paragraph enumerate exactly where a named party's position is vulnerable, and an auditor-response letter enumerates unannounced disputes before they reach a published account. Third, and unique to this row, THE CONCLUSION IS UNSAFE TO EXCERPT: assumptions and qualifications are load-bearing, so a compact dossier or a summary that carries the operative sentence without them does not merely leak, it misstates - so this row's redaction rule is that a conclusion travels with its bounds or it does not travel. No handling class is assigned; P7 owns that vocabulary, and the product decides no question of privilege, waiver, disclosure right or legal effect.
open_question: Where advice and instructions are bound into one PDF, the schema anchor's COUNSEL-INSTRUCTION signal and this row's advice structure both fire on the same bytes; R1c should record which template holds the combined artefact rather than leaving two rows to claim it. Separately, `addressee` is proposed with its own decline recommendation attached - see proposed_fields - and NJ-OA-1 through NJ-OA-4 in the memo.
